Each fused-star block derivative is an attainable weighted averaging matrix for arbitrary independently positive edge penalties. Discrete coarea reduces the exact Gini operator norm to binary cuts. The proposed bound is verified by a concave quadratic endpoint reduction in free-leaf count; remaining hub-in and hub-out cuts give exact B_r and C_r formulas and explicit witnesses. Optimizing these formulas establishes the reciprocal stability interval, penalty invariance, and extreme-mass envelope. The unrestricted analytic proof is corroborated by exact rational local-cut and independently evaluated proximal two-input tests.

value.rationale: Fused quadratic graph denoising is a standard stable inverse problem, yet strong Hilbert stability does not determine unweighted pairwise-dispersion stability. The new formula gives sharp all-size mass tolerances, shows an otherwise surprising independence from every positive fusion-edge weight, produces real extremizing data pairs, and distinguishes low-hub-mass and high-hub-mass instability mechanisms with a five-leaf crossover. These natural structural stability boundaries are more informative than a small numerical example.
